```{r birds}

birds <- read.csv('/Users/meganyoumans/Desktop/Adelphi Coursework/Statistical Modeling/Datasets 2/Datasets/Isolation.csv')
library(AICcmodavg)
library(ggplot2)
summary(birds)

##indicence, area, isolation 

bird1 <- lm(birds$incidence ~ 1)
bird2 <- lm(birds$incidence ~ birds$area)
bird3 <- lm(birds$incidence ~ birds$isolation)
bird4 <- lm(birds$incidence ~ birds$area * birds$isolation)
bird5 <- lm(birds$incidence ~ birds$area + birds$isolation)

AICc(bird1)
AICc(bird2)
AICc(bird3)
AICc(bird4)
AICc(bird5)

##[1] 75.53779
##[1] 59.49274
##[1] 45.55016
##[1] 38.92573
##[1] 39.21524

##Bird4 looks to be the best fit model with the lowest AICc number of the tests.

AICc(bird1) - AICc(bird4)
AICc(bird2) - AICc(bird4)
AICc(bird3) - AICc(bird4)
AICc(bird4) - AICc(bird4)
AICc(bird5) - AICc(bird4)

##[1] 36.61206
##[1] 20.56701
##[1] 6.624427
##[1] 0
##[1] 0.2895125

##bird4 followed by bird 5 are the best fit models for this data set as they are closest to 0, followed by bird 3. 

delta1 <- AICc(bird1) - AICc(bird4)
delta2 <- AICc(bird2) - AICc(bird4)
delta3 <- AICc(bird3) - AICc(bird4)
delta4 <- AICc(bird4) - AICc(bird4)
delta5 <- AICc(bird5) - AICc(bird4)

summary(bird4)
summary(bird5)

par(mfrow = c(1,2)) ##set up the stwo side by side plots 
boxplot(birds$area,birds$incidence, data = birds, xlab = "incidence", ylab="area")
boxplot(birds$isolation,birds$incidence, data = birds, xlab="incidence", ylab="isolation")

birdplot <- glm(incidence ~ area * isolation, family = binomial, data = birds)

plot(birds$area, birds$incidence,
     xlab="Area",
     ylab="Incidence",
    main="Regression Curve", pch = 16, col = "blue")

ggplot(birds, aes(x=birds$area, y=birds$incidence)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5, position = position_jitter(height = 0.02)) + ##jitter keeps points slightly separate
  geom_smooth(method = "glm", method.args = list(family = "binomial"), se = TRUE) +
  labs(title = "Regression Curve",
         x="Area",
       y="Incidence")+
  theme_minimal() ##removes a checkered background to be more visually appealing


```

Note that the `echo = FALSE` parameter was added to the code chunk to prevent printing of the R code that generated the plot.
